author: blu
body: The emitter is an Emit-quire function, and this chapter names it without citing anything. That is what the concatenated unit allows -- Emit sorts before Types, so these are backward references -- and the reverse direction is ordinary too: `boot-cap-mask-for` in the X86-64 Chapter reads `cap-bits-for-name` out of the foreword, and `capability-vocabulary` here in Types is a projection of that same table.

author: blu
body: The unary form has an x86 emitter too: a process-table exit-status cell, written by `process-exit`'s helper and by `__proc_entry` from the closure's return value, delivered to a waiter through its saved RAX by the exit wake loop, and answered by `process-wait` -- so a child's exit status means the same thing on bare metal as on the hosts.

author: reek
body: All three are here now, one row each. `builtin-names` is the names in it; `builtin-type-env` is a fold of `env-bind` over the ones that carry a type; `x86-builtin-emitters` is the rows whose `bs-emit` is a `Just`, and the routing list is derived from that in turn, so being routed IS having an emitter. None of the three is written out by hand any more, so none of them can drift from this one. The build-time guard that used to reconcile the emitter column with the rest had nothing left to compare and is deleted.

author: reek
body: Eight names carry no type, and each is deliberate. `True`, `False` and `Nothing` are special-cased by the checker -- that is how CDX2086 gets to say that Nothing is a type and not a value. `open-file`, `close-file`, `read-all`, `now` and `random-integer` are effect operations, typed by their `effect` declarations rather than here. A name with no type resolves and is not bound; that is what `None` means in this table, and it is a statement rather than an omission.

author: reek
body: The order is the order the let-chain bound in, and it is load-bearing: `env-bind` REPLACES, so where a name appears twice the LAST one wins. No name appears twice now. `process-exit` did, with two different types, and the nullary one bound second and won -- so `process-exit 0` answered CDX2001, Integer vs Fun, and the unary form every transpiler emitter implements was unreachable. The fix is two names for what were always two operations:

author: reek
body: `process-exit` is the host form, `Integer -> [Process] Nothing`. It is what `std::process::exit`, `Environment.Exit` and `sys.exit` mean, and the 53 plugs emit it under this name.

author: reek
body: `process-exit-self` is the bare-metal form and takes no argument. It is the syscall `emit-process-exit-helper` writes: mark this slot FREE, walk the wake loop marking every waiter READY, jump to `__idle_dispatch`. Its neighbours `process-yield`, `process-wait` and `get-ticks` are the same nullary shape, which is the family it belongs to.

author: reek
body: bs-varies answers whether two calls with the same arguments can differ, either by returning a different value or by touching the machine. A new builtin takes True, and takes it without argument: the cost of a wrong True is an optimisation nobody gets, and the cost of a wrong False is a frozen clock or a constant hardware-random.

author: reek
body: A definition with no parameters is compiled as a function, so naming it calls it and its body runs again. It is a genuine constant only when running it twice cannot differ, which bs-varies decides for every builtin the body reaches.

author: reek
body: Three answers here are deliberately conservative, because a wrong True costs an optimisation and a wrong False costs a miscompile. An expression shape the walk does not enumerate answers varies, which covers act, match, handle, try, fork, await and field-store without naming them. A user function is descended into on fuel, and running out answers varies, which is what makes the walk total against recursion. A lambda is judged by what it CAPTURES and not by what its body does: the body runs when the closure is called, not when the constant is built, so a closure over nothing is as constant as an integer.

author: reek
body: The set of definitions whose bodies cannot vary is a LEAST fixpoint, grown from empty. That direction is the safe one: a def only joins the set once everything it names is already in it, so stopping early under-approximates and costs an optimisation rather than correctness.
